content.text: In a single solution containing 1 mM Cu(II), 1 mM Fe(III), 10 mM citrate, 10 mM glycine, 0.1 M chloride, and 0.1 M ammonia at 25 C and I=0.1 m, build the joint two-dimensional E-pH Pourbaix diagram over pH 0-14 and E=-1.0 to +1.5 V_SHE. Identify how Cu and Fe partition among species, and report the principal region boundaries and junctions using the equilibrium constants and potentials actually used by the solver.

1	---
     2	name: frontend-design
     3	description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
     4	license: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt
     5	---
     6	
     7	# Frontend Design
     8	
     9	Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.
    10	
    11	## Ground your designs in the subject matter
    12	
    13	If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.
    14	
    15	## Design principles
    16	
    17	For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.
    18	
    19	Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.
    20	
    21	Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.
    22	
    23	Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.
    24	
    25	Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
    26	- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
    27	- Using all caps for labels.
    28	- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.
    29	
    30	Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.
    31	
    32	Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.
    33	
    34	Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.
    35	
    36	## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique
    37	
    38	For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
    39	1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
    40	2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
    41	3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
    42	4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
    43	5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.
    44	
    45	All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.
    46	
    47	Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
    48	- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
    49	- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
    50	- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
    51	- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.
    52	
    53	Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.
    54	
    55	When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.
    56	
    57	## Restraint and self-critique
    58	
    59	Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.
    60	
    61	## More on writing in design
    62	
    63	Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.
    64	
    65	Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.
    66	
    67	Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.
    68	
    69	Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.
    70	
    71	Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.
    72

"""

Components (mass-balance): Cu2+, Fe3+, Cit3-, Gly-, Cl-, NH3 ; fixed: H+ (pH), e- (pe), H2O.

Species concentrations: C_i = 10^( logK_i + sum_j a_ij log a_j - log gamma_i )

import numpy as np

F_RT = 0.059159  # V per log unit at 25 C
COMP = ['Cu', 'Fe', 'Cit', 'Gly', 'Cl', 'NH3', 'H', 'e']
NC = 6                     # mass-balance components
Z_COMP = np.array([2, 3, -3, -1, -1, 0])
T_TOT = np.array([1e-3, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-2, 0.1, 0.1])   # mol/L
I_STR = 0.1
A_DH = 0.5085

def log_gamma(z, I=I_STR):
    sI = np.sqrt(I)
    return -A_DH * z**2 * (sI/(1+sI) - 0.3*I)

MINTEQ = 'MINTEQ v4 database (PHREEQC distribution)'
NIST = 'NIST SRD 46 (Smith & Martell), I=0.1; charge-neutral steps, I-correction negligible'
SP = []
def add(name, st, logk, z, state=None, src=MINTEQ, note=''):
    SP.append(dict(name=name, st=st, logK=float(logk), z=z, state=state, src=src, note=note))

# free components
add('Cu2+', {'Cu':1}, 0.0, 2, 'Cu2', 'component')
add('Fe3+', {'Fe':1}, 0.0, 3, 'Fe3', 'component')
add('Cit3-', {'Cit':1}, 0.0, -3, None, 'component')
add('Gly-', {'Gly':1}, 0.0, -1, None, 'component')
add('Cl-', {'Cl':1}, 0.0, -1, None, 'component')
add('NH3', {'NH3':1}, 0.0, 0, None, 'component')
# ligand protonation
add('HCit2-', {'Cit':1,'H':1}, 6.396, -2)
add('H2Cit-', {'Cit':1,'H':2}, 11.157, -1)
add('H3Cit', {'Cit':1,'H':3}, 14.285, 0)
add('HGly (zwitterion)', {'Gly':1,'H':1}, 9.778, 0)
add('H2Gly+', {'Gly':1,'H':2}, 12.128, 1)
add('NH4+', {'NH3':1,'H':1}, 9.244, 1)
# redox master species
add('Cu+', {'Cu':1,'e':1}, 2.69, 1, 'Cu1', MINTEQ, 'E0(Cu2+/Cu+) = 0.159 V')
add('Fe2+', {'Fe':1,'e':1}, 13.032, 2, 'Fe2', MINTEQ, 'E0(Fe3+/Fe2+) = 0.771 V')
add('FeO4^2-', {'Fe':1,'H':-8,'e':-3}, -3*2.20/F_RT, -2, 'Fe6', 'Wood 1958 / Pourbaix: E0(FeO4^2-/Fe3+) = 2.20 V', 'less certain')
add('HFeO4-', {'Fe':1,'H':-7,'e':-3}, -3*2.20/F_RT + 7.3, -1, 'Fe6', 'pKa(HFeO4-) = 7.3', 'less certain')
# Cu(II) hydrolysis
add('CuOH+', {'Cu':1,'H':-1}, -7.497, 1, 'Cu2')
add('Cu(OH)2(aq)', {'Cu':1,'H':-2}, -16.194, 0, 'Cu2')
add('Cu(OH)3-', {'Cu':1,'H':-3}, -26.879, -1, 'Cu2')
add('Cu(OH)4^2-', {'Cu':1,'H':-4}, -39.98, -2, 'Cu2')
add('Cu2(OH)2^2+', {'Cu':2,'H':-2}, -10.594, 2, 'Cu2')
# Cu(II) chloride
add('CuCl+', {'Cu':1,'Cl':1}, 0.2, 1, 'Cu2')
add('CuCl2(aq)', {'Cu':1,'Cl':2}, -0.26, 0, 'Cu2')
add('CuCl3-', {'Cu':1,'Cl':3}, -2.29, -1, 'Cu2')
add('CuCl4^2-', {'Cu':1,'Cl':4}, -4.59, -2, 'Cu2')
# Cu(II) ammines
add('Cu(NH3)^2+', {'Cu':1,'NH3':1}, 4.04, 2, 'Cu2', NIST)
add('Cu(NH3)2^2+', {'Cu':1,'NH3':2}, 7.47, 2, 'Cu2', NIST)
add('Cu(NH3)3^2+', {'Cu':1,'NH3':3}, 10.27, 2, 'Cu2', NIST)
add('Cu(NH3)4^2+', {'Cu':1,'NH3':4}, 11.75, 2, 'Cu2', NIST)
# Cu(II) citrate
add('CuCit-', {'Cu':1,'Cit':1}, 7.57, -1, 'Cu2')
add('Cu(Cit)2^4-', {'Cu':1,'Cit':2}, 8.9, -4, 'Cu2')
add('CuHCit', {'Cu':1,'Cit':1,'H':1}, 10.87, 0, 'Cu2')
add('CuH2Cit+', {'Cu':1,'Cit':1,'H':2}, 13.23, 1, 'Cu2')
add('Cu2(Cit)2^2-', {'Cu':2,'Cit':2}, 16.9, -2, 'Cu2')
# Cu(II) glycinate
add('CuGly+', {'Cu':1,'Gly':1}, 8.57, 1, 'Cu2')
add('Cu(Gly)2', {'Cu':1,'Gly':2}, 15.7, 0, 'Cu2')
# Cu(I) complexes  (formation from Cu2+ + e-)
add('CuCl(aq)', {'Cu':1,'e':1,'Cl':1}, 2.69+3.1, 0, 'Cu1')
add('CuCl2-', {'Cu':1,'e':1,'Cl':2}, 2.69+5.42, -1, 'Cu1')
add('CuCl3^2-', {'Cu':1,'e':1,'Cl':3}, 2.69+4.75, -2, 'Cu1')
add('Cu(NH3)+', {'Cu':1,'e':1,'NH3':1}, 2.69+5.93, 1, 'Cu1', NIST)
add('Cu(NH3)2+', {'Cu':1,'e':1,'NH3':2}, 2.69+10.86, 1, 'Cu1', NIST)
add('Cu(Gly)2-', {'Cu':1,'e':1,'Gly':2}, 2.69+10.3, -1, 'Cu1')
# Fe(III) hydrolysis / chloride
add('FeOH^2+', {'Fe':1,'H':-1}, -2.187, 2, 'Fe3')
add('Fe(OH)2+', {'Fe':1,'H':-2}, -4.594, 1, 'Fe3')
add('Fe(OH)3(aq)', {'Fe':1,'H':-3}, -12.56, 0, 'Fe3')
add('Fe(OH)4-', {'Fe':1,'H':-4}, -21.588, -1, 'Fe3')
add('Fe2(OH)2^4+', {'Fe':2,'H':-2}, -2.854, 4, 'Fe3')
add('Fe3(OH)4^5+', {'Fe':3,'H':-4}, -6.288, 5, 'Fe3')
add('FeCl^2+', {'Fe':1,'Cl':1}, 1.48, 2, 'Fe3')
add('FeCl2+', {'Fe':1,'Cl':2}, 2.13, 1, 'Fe3')
add('FeCl3(aq)', {'Fe':1,'Cl':3}, 1.13, 0, 'Fe3')
# Fe(III) citrate / glycinate
add('FeCit', {'Fe':1,'Cit':1}, 13.1, 0, 'Fe3')
add('FeHCit+', {'Fe':1,'Cit':1,'H':1}, 14.4, 1, 'Fe3')
add('Fe(OH)Cit-', {'Fe':1,'Cit':1,'H':-1}, 13.1-2.6, -1, 'Fe3',
    'added: FeCit deprotonation pKa = 2.6 (Timberlake 1964; Koenigsberger et al. 2000)', 'less certain')
add('FeGly^2+', {'Fe':1,'Gly':1}, 9.38, 2, 'Fe3')
add('FeHGly^3+', {'Fe':1,'Gly':1,'H':1}, 11.55, 3, 'Fe3')
# Fe(II)  (formation from Fe3+ + e-)
add('FeOH+', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'H':-1}, 13.032-9.397, 1, 'Fe2')
add('Fe(OH)2(aq)', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'H':-2}, 13.032-20.494, 0, 'Fe2')
add('Fe(OH)3-', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'H':-3}, 13.032-28.991, -1, 'Fe2')
add('FeCl+', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'Cl':1}, 13.032+0.14, 1, 'Fe2', 'WATEQ4F database')
add('FeCit-', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'Cit':1}, 13.032+6.1, -1, 'Fe2')
add('FeHCit', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'Cit':1,'H':1}, 13.032+10.2, 0, 'Fe2')
add('FeGly+', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'Gly':1}, 13.032+4.31, 1, 'Fe2')
add('Fe(Gly)2', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'Gly':2}, 13.032+8.29, 0, 'Fe2')
add('Fe(NH3)^2+', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'NH3':1}, 13.032+1.4, 2, 'Fe2', NIST)
add('Fe(NH3)2^2+', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'NH3':2}, 13.032+2.2, 2, 'Fe2', NIST)

# Solids: formation from components, activity = 1
SOL = []
def adds(name, st, logk, state, src=MINTEQ, note=''):
    SOL.append(dict(name=name, st=st, logK=float(logk), state=state, src=src, note=note))
adds('Cu(s)', {'Cu':1,'e':2}, 2.69+8.756, 'Cu0', MINTEQ, 'E0(Cu2+/Cu) = 0.339 V, E0(Cu+/Cu) = 0.518 V')
adds('Cu2O(s) cuprite', {'Cu':2,'e':2,'H':-2}, 2*2.69+1.406, 'Cu1', MINTEQ, 'Cu2O + 2H+ = 2Cu+ + H2O, log K = -1.406')
adds('CuO(s) tenorite', {'Cu':1,'H':-2}, -7.644, 'Cu2', MINTEQ, 'CuO + 2H+ = Cu2+ + H2O, log K = 7.644')
adds('CuCl(s) nantokite', {'Cu':1,'e':1,'Cl':1}, 2.69+6.73, 'Cu1', MINTEQ, 'CuCl = Cu+ + Cl-, log K = -6.73')
adds('Fe(s)', {'Fe':1,'e':3}, 13.032-15.11, 'Fe0', 'CRC: E0(Fe2+/Fe) = -0.447 V', '')
adds('Fe(OH)3(s) ferrihydrite', {'Fe':1,'H':-3}, -3.191, 'Fe3', MINTEQ, 'Fe(OH)3 + 3H+ = Fe3+ + 3H2O, log K = 3.191')
adds('Fe(OH)2(s)', {'Fe':1,'e':1,'H':-2}, 13.032-13.564, 'Fe2', MINTEQ, 'Fe(OH)2 + 2H+ = Fe2+ + 2H2O, log K = 13.564')

NS = len(SP); NSOL = len(SOL)
A = np.zeros((NS, 8)); LOGK = np.zeros(NS); Z = np.zeros(NS); LG = np.zeros(NS)
for i, s in enumerate(SP):
    for k, v in s['st'].items():
        A[i, COMP.index(k)] = v
    LOGK[i] = s['logK']; Z[i] = s['z']; LG[i] = log_gamma(s['z'])
AS = np.zeros((NSOL, 8)); LOGKS = np.zeros(NSOL)
for i, s in enumerate(SOL):
    for k, v in s['st'].items():
        AS[i, COMP.index(k)] = v
    LOGKS[i] = s['logK']
LGC = log_gamma(Z_COMP)          # component activity coefficients
AM = A[:, :NC]; ASM = AS[:, :NC]
LN10 = np.log(10.0)

def species_logC(x, pH, pe):
    """x = log10 free concentrations of the 6 components."""
    loga = np.concatenate([x + LGC, [-pH, -pe]])
    return LOGK + A @ loga - LG

def solid_SI(x, pH, pe):
    loga = np.concatenate([x + LGC, [-pH, -pe]])
    return LOGKS + AS @ loga

def newton(x0, present, pH, pe, T=T_TOT, maxit=300, tol=1e-10):
    x = x0.copy()
    pres = list(present)
    n = np.zeros(len(pres))
    for it in range(maxit):
        logC = species_logC(x, pH, pe)
        C = 10.0**np.clip(logC, -300, 30)
        tot = AM.T @ C                                   # (6,)
        if pres:
            tot = tot + ASM[pres].T @ n
        F = tot / T - 1.0
        Fs = solid_SI(x, pH, pe)[pres] if pres else np.zeros(0)
        if np.max(np.abs(F)) < tol and (len(Fs) == 0 or np.max(np.abs(Fs)) < tol):
            return x, n, True, it
        # Jacobian
        J11 = LN10 * (AM.T * C) @ AM / T[:, None]        # dF_j/dx_k
        m = len(pres)
        J = np.zeros((NC+m, NC+m))
        J[:NC, :NC] = J11
        if m:
            J[:NC, NC:] = ASM[pres].T / T[:, None]
            J[NC:, :NC] = ASM[pres]
        rhs = -np.concatenate([F, Fs])
        try:
            d = np.linalg.solve(J, rhs)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            d = np.linalg.lstsq(J, rhs, rcond=None)[0]
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(d)):
            return x, n, False, it
        step = np.max(np.abs(d[:NC]))
        if step > 1.0:
            d = d / step
        x = x + d[:NC]
        if m:
            n = n + d[NC:]
    return x, n, False, maxit

def solve_point(pH, E, x0=None, present0=(), T=T_TOT):
    pe = E / F_RT
    if x0 is None:
        x0 = np.log10(T) - np.array([4, 4, 1, 1, 0.1, 0.5])
    present = list(present0)
    tried = set()
    x = x0.copy()
    for outer in range(15):
        x, n, ok, it = newton(x, present, pH, pe, T)
        if not ok:
            # retry from cold start with the same phase set
            x, n, ok, it = newton(np.log10(T) - np.array([4, 4, 1, 1, 0.1, 0.5]), present, pH, pe, T)
            if not ok:
                x, n, ok, it = newton(np.log10(T) - np.array([12, 12, 1, 1, 0.1, 0.5]), present, pH, pe, T)
            if not ok:
                return None
        # phase rule: remove any solid with negative amount
        if present and np.min(n) < 0:
            k = int(np.argmin(n))
            tried.add(tuple(sorted(present)))
            present.pop(k)
            continue
        SI = solid_SI(x, pH, pe)
        absent = [s for s in range(NSOL) if s not in present]
        if absent:
            k = max(absent, key=lambda s: SI[s])
            if SI[k] > 1e-8:
                cand = tuple(sorted(present + [k]))
                if cand in tried:
                    # avoid cycling: try the next-best candidate
                    others = sorted(absent, key=lambda s: -SI[s])
                    cand2 = None
                    for o in others:
                        if SI[o] > 1e-8 and tuple(sorted(present+[o])) not in tried:
                            cand2 = o; break
                    if cand2 is None:
                        break
                    k = cand2
                tried.add(tuple(sorted(present)))
                present.append(k)
                continue
        return dict(x=x, n=n, present=present, pe=pe, it=it)
    return dict(x=x, n=n, present=present, pe=pe, it=it)

def speciation(res, pH, T=T_TOT):
    """Return per-species concentrations and per-metal shares."""
    logC = species_logC(res['x'], pH, res['pe'])
    C = 10.0**np.clip(logC, -300, 30)
    out = {}
    for j, met in enumerate(['Cu', 'Fe']):
        shares = {}
        for i in range(NS):
            if AM[i, j] != 0:
                shares[SP[i]['name']] = AM[i, j] * C[i] / T[j]
        for kk, s in enumerate(res['present']):
            if ASM[s, j] != 0:
                shares[SOL[s]['name']] = ASM[s, j] * res['n'][kk] / T[j]
        out[met] = shares
    return C, out

STATE_OF = {}
for s in SP: STATE_OF[s['name']] = s['state']
for s in SOL: STATE_OF[s['name']] = s['state']

cd /home/claude && cat > run_grid.py << 'EOF'
import numpy as np, time, pickle
from pourbaix import *
pHs = np.round(np.arange(0, 14.0001, 0.05), 3)
Es  = np.round(np.arange(-1.0, 1.5001, 0.01), 3)
nP, nE = len(pHs), len(Es)
names = [s['name'] for s in SP] + [s['name'] for s in SOL]
name_idx = {n:i for i,n in enumerate(names)}
lab = np.zeros((2, nE, nP), dtype=np.int16)
frac = np.zeros((2, nE, nP), dtype=np.float32)
top = np.zeros((2, 3, nE, nP), dtype=np.int16); topf = np.zeros((2, 3, nE, nP), dtype=np.float32)
ox = np.zeros((7, nE, nP), dtype=np.float32)   # Cu0,Cu1,Cu2,Fe0,Fe2,Fe3,Fe6
solids = np.zeros((NSOL, nE, nP), dtype=bool)
xfree = np.zeros((NC, nE, nP), dtype=np.float32)
fails = []
oxkeys = ['Cu0','Cu1','Cu2','Fe0','Fe2','Fe3','Fe6']
t0 = time.time()
prev_col = None
for ip, pH in enumerate(pHs):
    col = [None]*nE
    for ie, E in enumerate(Es):
        guesses = []
        if ie > 0 and col[ie-1] is not None: guesses.append(col[ie-1])
        if prev_col is not None and prev_col[ie] is not None: guesses.append(prev_col[ie])
        guesses.append(None)
        r = None
        for g in guesses:
            if g is None: r = solve_point(pH, E)
            else: r = solve_point(pH, E, x0=g['x'], present0=g['present'])
            if r is not None:
                # verify mass balance
                logC = species_logC(r['x'], pH, r['pe']); Cc = 10**np.clip(logC,-300,30)
                tot = AM.T@Cc + (ASM[r['present']].T@r['n'] if r['present'] else 0)
                if np.max(np.abs(tot/T_TOT-1)) < 1e-6 and (len(r['n'])==0 or np.min(r['n'])>=-1e-15): break
                r = None
        if r is None:
            fails.append((pH,E)); continue
        col[ie] = r
        C, sh = speciation(r, pH)
        for j, met in enumerate(['Cu','Fe']):
            items = sorted(sh[met].items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])
            lab[j, ie, ip] = name_idx[items[0][0]]; frac[j, ie, ip] = items[0][1]
            for k in range(3):
                top[j,k,ie,ip] = name_idx[items[k][0]]; topf[j,k,ie,ip] = items[k][1]
            for nm, v in items:
                st = STATE_OF[nm]
                if st in oxkeys: ox[oxkeys.index(st), ie, ip] += v
        for s in r['present']: solids[s, ie, ip] = True
        xfree[:, ie, ip] = r['x']
    prev_col = col
    if ip % 20 == 0: print(f"pH {pH:5.2f} done, {time.time()-t0:6.1f}s, fails so far {len(fails)}", flush=True)
print('total time', time.time()-t0, 'fails', len(fails))
np.savez_compressed('grid.npz', pHs=pHs, Es=Es, lab=lab, frac=frac, top=top, topf=topf, ox=ox, solids=solids, xfree=xfree, names=np.array(names))
pickle.dump(fails, open('fails.pkl','wb'))
EOF
nohup python3 run_grid.py > run_grid.log 2>&1 &
sleep 45; cat run_grid.log

import numpy as np, collections, json
d=np.load('grid.npz', allow_pickle=True)
names=list(d['names']); lab=d['lab']; pHs=d['pHs']; Es=d['Es']; frac=d['frac']; solids=d['solids']; ox=d['ox']
nE,nP=lab.shape[1:]
dp, dE = 0.05, 0.01
def boundaries(L):
    pts=collections.defaultdict(list)
    # horizontal neighbours (pH direction)
    a=L[:,:-1]; b=L[:,1:]
    ii,jj=np.where(a!=b)
    for i,j in zip(ii,jj):
        key=tuple(sorted((int(a[i,j]),int(b[i,j]))))
        pts[key].append((pHs[j]+dp/2, Es[i]))
    a=L[:-1,:]; b=L[1:,:]
    ii,jj=np.where(a!=b)
    for i,j in zip(ii,jj):
        key=tuple(sorted((int(a[i,j]),int(b[i,j]))))
        pts[key].append((pHs[j], Es[i]+dE/2))
    return pts
def junctions(L):
    out=[]
    for i in range(nE-1):
        for j in range(nP-1):
            s=set([int(L[i,j]),int(L[i,j+1]),int(L[i+1,j]),int(L[i+1,j+1])])
            if len(s)>=3: out.append((tuple(sorted(s)), pHs[j]+dp/2, Es[i]+dE/2))
    # cluster by label set and proximity
    clusters=[]
    for key,p,e in out:
        for c in clusters:
            if c['key']==key and abs(c['pH']-p)<0.4 and abs(c['E']-e)<0.08:
                c['pts'].append((p,e)); c['pH']=np.mean([q[0] for q in c['pts']]); c['E']=np.mean([q[1] for q in c['pts']]); break
        else:
            clusters.append(dict(key=key,pH=p,E=e,pts=[(p,e)]))
    return clusters
report={}
for j,met in enumerate(['Cu','Fe']):
    L=lab[j]
    B=boundaries(L)
    rows=[]
    for key,p in sorted(B.items(), key=lambda kv:-len(kv[1])):
        p=np.array(p); n=len(p)
        if n<6: continue
        pr=(p[:,0].min(),p[:,0].max()); er=(p[:,1].min(),p[:,1].max())
        kind=''; eq=''
        if pr[1]-pr[0] < 0.12:
            kind='acid-base (vertical)'; eq=f"pH = {p[:,0].mean():.2f}"
        elif er[1]-er[0] < 0.015:
            kind='redox (horizontal)'; eq=f"E = {p[:,1].mean():+.3f} V"
        else:
            # fit E = a + b pH
            A=np.vstack([np.ones(n),p[:,0]]).T
            (a,b),res,_,_=np.linalg.lstsq(A,p[:,1],rcond=None)
            rms=np.sqrt(np.mean((A@[a,b]-p[:,1])**2))
            kind='redox (sloping)'; eq=f"E = {a:+.3f} {b:+.4f}·pH  (rms {rms*1000:.0f} mV)"
            if rms>0.012: kind='redox (curved)'
        # sample points at 5 pH values
        samp=[]
        for q in np.linspace(pr[0],pr[1],5):
            k=np.argmin(np.abs(p[:,0]-q)); samp.append((round(float(p[k,0]),2),round(float(p[k,1]),3)))
        rows.append(dict(a=names[key[0]],b=names[key[1]],n=int(n),pH=[round(float(x),2) for x in pr],E=[round(float(x),3) for x in er],kind=kind,eq=eq,samples=samp))
    J=junctions(L)
    jr=[dict(species=[names[k] for k in c['key']],pH=round(float(c['pH']),2),E=round(float(c['E']),3),n=len(c['pts'])) for c in J]
    report[met]=dict(boundaries=rows,junctions=jr)
    print('=====',met,'boundaries (>=6 pts):')
    for r in rows: print(f"  {r['a']:24s} | {r['b']:24s} n={r['n']:4d} pH {r['pH']} E {r['E']} {r['kind']:22s} {r['eq']}")
    print('  junctions:')
    for r in jr: print('   ',r)
# joint crossings: junctions of the joint label
JL = lab[0].astype(np.int64)*1000 + lab[1].astype(np.int64)
Jj = junctions(JL)
cross=[]
cuJ=set((round(c['pH'],1),round(c['E'],2)) for c in report['Cu']['junctions']); 
for c in Jj:
    cu=set(k//1000 for k in c['key']); fe=set(k%1000 for k in c['key'])
    if len(cu)>=2 and len(fe)>=2:
        cross.append(dict(Cu=[names[k] for k in sorted(cu)],Fe=[names[k] for k in sorted(fe)],pH=round(float(c['pH']),2),E=round(float(c['E']),3)))
report['crossings']=cross
print('===== Cu/Fe boundary crossings:', len(cross))
for c in cross: print('   ',c)
# oxidation-state shares along a few pH values
json.dump(report, open('report.json','w'), indent=1)
EOF

input.description: Plotting script: joint, Cu-only and Fe-only E-pH diagrams as SVG (and PNG previews)
input.file_text:
import numpy as np, json, collections
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
from scipy import ndimage
plt.rcParams['svg.fonttype'] = 'none'
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'DejaVu Sans'

d = np.load('grid.npz', allow_pickle=True)
names = list(d['names']); lab = d['lab']; pHs = d['pHs']; Es = d['Es']
nE, nP = lab.shape[1:]
ext = [pHs[0]-0.025, pHs[-1]+0.025, Es[0]-0.005, Es[-1]+0.005]

STATE = json.load(open('states.json'))   # name -> state
PRETTY = json.load(open('pretty.json'))  # name -> display label (mathtext)

# ---- palettes by oxidation state (light fills) ----
CU_FILL = {'Cu0': ['#D8CDC2'], 'Cu1': ['#F5DDBE', '#F9E8D0', '#EFD2AC'],
           'Cu2': ['#F7D9D0', '#F2C9BB', '#FBE6DF', '#EDBCAA', '#F6D0C2', '#FCEEE8', '#E9B09C']}
FE_FILL = {'Fe0': ['#D3D9E0'], 'Fe2': ['#D3E3F3', '#C4D8EC', '#DFEBF7', '#B7CFE7', '#E6EFF9', '#CBDDF0', '#AFC9E3'],
           'Fe3': ['#DAD8EE', '#CCC9E6', '#E4E2F3', '#BFBBDE', '#D2CFE9', '#ECEAF7'],
           'Fe6': ['#E7D4F1', '#F0E2F7']}
CU_LINE, FE_LINE = '#9E4A16', '#26527F'
CU_TEXT, FE_TEXT = '#6E3410', '#1D3F63'

def assign_colors(L, fills):
    labs = [k for k, _ in collections.Counter(L.ravel()).most_common()]
    used = collections.defaultdict(int); cmap = {}
    for k in labs:
        st = STATE.get(names[k], 'Cu2')
        pal = fills[st]; cmap[k] = pal[used[st] % len(pal)]; used[st] += 1
    return cmap

def region_label_pos(mask):
    # distance transform in physical units (aspect-corrected)
    m = mask.astype(float)
    dt = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(m, sampling=[0.01/0.1, 0.05/1.0])  # E:0.1 V ~ pH:1
    i, j = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(dt), dt.shape)
    return pHs[j], Es[i], dt[i, j]

def draw_fills(ax, L, cmap):
    labs = sorted(cmap.keys())
    idx = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(labs)}
    img = np.vectorize(idx.get)(L)
    ax.imshow(img, origin='lower', extent=ext, aspect='auto', interpolation='nearest',
              cmap=ListedColormap([cmap[k] for k in labs]), vmin=-0.5, vmax=len(labs)-0.5, zorder=0)

def draw_lines(ax, L, color, lw=1.4, z=3):
    for k in np.unique(L):
        m = (L == k).astype(float)
        m = np.pad(m, 1, constant_values=0)
        X = np.concatenate([[pHs[0]-0.05], pHs, [pHs[-1]+0.05]])
        Y = np.concatenate([[Es[0]-0.01], Es, [Es[-1]+0.01]])
        ax.contour(X, Y, m, levels=[0.5], colors=[color], linewidths=lw, zorder=z)

def draw_labels(ax, L, color, min_area=0.0015, fs=10, italic=False):
    c = collections.Counter(L.ravel())
    for k, v in c.items():
        if v / L.size < min_area: continue
        m = (L == k)
        x, y, dist = region_label_pos(m)
        txt = PRETTY.get(names[k], names[k])
        fsz = fs if v/L.size > 0.01 else fs-2
        ax.text(x, y, txt, color=color, fontsize=fsz, ha='center', va='center',
                fontstyle='italic' if italic else 'normal', zorder=5,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.15', fc='white', ec='none', alpha=0.72))

def water(ax):
    x = np.array([0, 14])
    ax.plot(x, 1.229-0.05916*x, '--', color='#6B6B6B', lw=1, zorder=2)
    ax.plot(x, -0.05916*x, '--', color='#6B6B6B', lw=1, zorder=2)
    ax.text(0.25, 1.229-0.05916*0.25+0.03, 'O$_2$ / H$_2$O', color='#555', fontsize=8.5, rotation=-15, zorder=6)
    ax.text(0.25, -0.05916*0.25+0.03, 'H$_2$O / H$_2$', color='#555', fontsize=8.5, rotation=-15, zorder=6)

def frame(ax, title):
    ax.set_xlim(0, 14); ax.set_ylim(-1.0, 1.5)
    ax.set_xlabel('pH', fontsize=11); ax.set_ylabel('E / V vs SHE', fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xticks(range(0, 15, 1)); ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-1.0, 1.51, 0.25))
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11, loc='left', color='#222', pad=8)
    for s in ax.spines.values(): s.set_color('#444')

cu_cmap = assign_colors(lab[0], CU_FILL); fe_cmap = assign_colors(lab[1], FE_FILL)

# ---- Joint diagram ----
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 7.6), dpi=100)
draw_fills(ax, lab[0], cu_cmap)
draw_lines(ax, lab[0], CU_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_lines(ax, lab[1], FE_LINE, lw=1.6)
draw_labels(ax, lab[0], CU_TEXT, fs=10)
draw_labels(ax, lab[1], FE_TEXT, fs=9.5, italic=True)
water(ax)
frame(ax, 'Joint Cu/Fe E–pH predominance diagram: copper regions filled, copper boundaries in copper, iron boundaries and labels in blue')
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig('joint.svg', bbox_inches='tight'); fig.savefig('joint.png', dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
print('joint axes bbox (fig fraction):', ax.get_position().bounds)

# ---- Cu-only ----
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 7.6), dpi=100)
draw_fills(ax, lab[0], cu_cmap); draw_lines(ax, lab[0], CU_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_labels(ax, lab[0], CU_TEXT, fs=10.5, min_area=0.0003); water(ax)
frame(ax, 'Copper predominance (1 mM Cu total)')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('cu.svg', bbox_inches='tight'); fig.savefig('cu.png', dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')

# ---- Fe-only ----
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 7.6), dpi=100)
draw_fills(ax, lab[1], fe_cmap); draw_lines(ax, lab[1], FE_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_labels(ax, lab[1], FE_TEXT, fs=10.5, min_area=0.0003); water(ax)
frame(ax, 'Iron predominance (1 mM Fe total)')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('fe.svg', bbox_inches='tight'); fig.savefig('fe.png', dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
print('done')

import matplotlib

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
from scipy import ndimage
plt.rcParams['svg.fonttype'] = 'none'
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'DejaVu Sans'

d = np.load('grid.npz', allow_pickle=True)
names = list(d['names']); lab = d['lab']; pHs = d['pHs']; Es = d['Es']
nE, nP = lab.shape[1:]
ext = [pHs[0]-0.025, pHs[-1]+0.025, Es[0]-0.005, Es[-1]+0.005]

STATE = json.load(open('states.json'))   # name -> state
PRETTY = json.load(open('pretty.json'))  # name -> display label (mathtext)

# ---- palettes by oxidation state (light fills) ----
CU_FILL = {'Cu0': ['#D8CDC2'], 'Cu1': ['#F5DDBE', '#F9E8D0', '#EFD2AC'],
           'Cu2': ['#F7D9D0', '#F2C9BB', '#FBE6DF', '#EDBCAA', '#F6D0C2', '#FCEEE8', '#E9B09C']}
FE_FILL = {'Fe0': ['#D3D9E0'], 'Fe2': ['#D3E3F3', '#C4D8EC', '#DFEBF7', '#B7CFE7', '#E6EFF9', '#CBDDF0', '#AFC9E3'],
           'Fe3': ['#DAD8EE', '#CCC9E6', '#E4E2F3', '#BFBBDE', '#D2CFE9', '#ECEAF7'],
           'Fe6': ['#E7D4F1', '#F0E2F7']}
CU_LINE, FE_LINE = '#9E4A16', '#26527F'
CU_TEXT, FE_TEXT = '#6E3410', '#1D3F63'

def assign_colors(L, fills):
    labs = [k for k, _ in collections.Counter(L.ravel()).most_common()]
    used = collections.defaultdict(int); cmap = {}
    for k in labs:
        st = STATE.get(names[k], 'Cu2')
        pal = fills[st]; cmap[k] = pal[used[st] % len(pal)]; used[st] += 1
    return cmap

def region_label_pos(mask):
    # distance transform in physical units (aspect-corrected)
    m = mask.astype(float)
    dt = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(m, sampling=[0.01/0.1, 0.05/1.0])  # E:0.1 V ~ pH:1
    i, j = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(dt), dt.shape)
    return pHs[j], Es[i], dt[i, j]

def draw_fills(ax, L, cmap):
    labs = sorted(cmap.keys())
    idx = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(labs)}
    img = np.vectorize(idx.get)(L)
    ax.imshow(img, origin='lower', extent=ext, aspect='auto', interpolation='nearest',
              cmap=ListedColormap([cmap[k] for k in labs]), vmin=-0.5, vmax=len(labs)-0.5, zorder=0)

def draw_lines(ax, L, color, lw=1.4, z=3):
    for k in np.unique(L):
        m = (L == k).astype(float)
        m = np.pad(m, 1, constant_values=0)
        X = np.concatenate([[pHs[0]-0.05], pHs, [pHs[-1]+0.05]])
        Y = np.concatenate([[Es[0]-0.01], Es, [Es[-1]+0.01]])
        ax.contour(X, Y, m, levels=[0.5], colors=[color], linewidths=lw, zorder=z)

def draw_labels(ax, L, color, min_area=0.0015, fs=10, italic=False):
    c = collections.Counter(L.ravel())
    for k, v in c.items():
        if v / L.size < min_area: continue
        m = (L == k)
        x, y, dist = region_label_pos(m)
        txt = PRETTY.get(names[k], names[k])
        fsz = fs if v/L.size > 0.01 else fs-2
        ax.text(x, y, txt, color=color, fontsize=fsz, ha='center', va='center',
                fontstyle='italic' if italic else 'normal', zorder=5,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.15', fc='white', ec='none', alpha=0.72))

def water(ax):
    x = np.array([0, 14])
    ax.plot(x, 1.229-0.05916*x, '--', color='#6B6B6B', lw=1, zorder=2)
    ax.plot(x, -0.05916*x, '--', color='#6B6B6B', lw=1, zorder=2)
    ax.text(0.25, 1.229-0.05916*0.25+0.03, 'O$_2$ / H$_2$O', color='#555', fontsize=8.5, rotation=-15, zorder=6)
    ax.text(0.25, -0.05916*0.25+0.03, 'H$_2$O / H$_2$', color='#555', fontsize=8.5, rotation=-15, zorder=6)

def frame(ax, title):
    ax.set_xlim(0, 14); ax.set_ylim(-1.0, 1.5)
    ax.set_xlabel('pH', fontsize=11); ax.set_ylabel('E / V vs SHE', fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xticks(range(0, 15, 1)); ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-1.0, 1.51, 0.25))
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=11, loc='left', color='#222', pad=8)
    for s in ax.spines.values(): s.set_color('#444')

cu_cmap = assign_colors(lab[0], CU_FILL); fe_cmap = assign_colors(lab[1], FE_FILL)

# ---- Joint diagram ----
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 7.6), dpi=100)
draw_fills(ax, lab[0], cu_cmap)
draw_lines(ax, lab[0], CU_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_lines(ax, lab[1], FE_LINE, lw=1.6)
draw_labels(ax, lab[0], CU_TEXT, fs=10)
draw_labels(ax, lab[1], FE_TEXT, fs=9.5, italic=True)
water(ax)
frame(ax, 'Joint Cu/Fe E–pH predominance diagram: copper regions filled, copper boundaries in copper, iron boundaries and labels in blue')
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig('joint.svg', bbox_inches='tight'); fig.savefig('joint.png', dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
print('joint axes bbox (fig fraction):', ax.get_position().bounds)

# ---- Cu-only ----
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 7.6), dpi=100)
draw_fills(ax, lab[0], cu_cmap); draw_lines(ax, lab[0], CU_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_labels(ax, lab[0], CU_TEXT, fs=10.5, min_area=0.0003); water(ax)
frame(ax, 'Copper predominance (1 mM Cu total)')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('cu.svg', bbox_inches='tight'); fig.savefig('cu.png', dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')

# ---- Fe-only ----
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 7.6), dpi=100)
draw_fills(ax, lab[1], fe_cmap); draw_lines(ax, lab[1], FE_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_labels(ax, lab[1], FE_TEXT, fs=10.5, min_area=0.0003); water(ax)
frame(ax, 'Iron predominance (1 mM Fe total)')
fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig('fe.svg', bbox_inches='tight'); fig.savefig('fe.png', dpi=110, bbox_inches='tight')
print('done')

import numpy as np, json, collections, glob
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.font_manager as fm
for f in sorted(glob.glob('/home/claude/fonts/*.ttf')):
    fm.fontManager.addfont(f)
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
from scipy import ndimage

plt.rcParams.update({
    'svg.fonttype': 'path',
    'font.family': 'IBM Plex Sans',
    'mathtext.fontset': 'custom',
    'mathtext.rm': 'IBM Plex Sans',
    'mathtext.it': 'IBM Plex Sans:italic',
    'mathtext.bf': 'IBM Plex Sans:medium',
    'mathtext.default': 'regular',
    'axes.unicode_minus': True,
})

d = np.load('grid.npz', allow_pickle=True)
names = list(d['names']); lab = d['lab']; pHs = d['pHs']; Es = d['Es']
nE, nP = lab.shape[1:]
dpH, dE = 0.05, 0.01
ext = [pHs[0]-dpH/2, pHs[-1]+dpH/2, Es[0]-dE/2, Es[-1]+dE/2]

STATE = json.load(open('states.json'))
PRETTY = json.load(open('pretty.json'))

CU_FILL = {'Cu0': ['#DCD3C9'], 'Cu1': ['#F4DCBA', '#F8E6CC', '#EED0A6'],
           'Cu2': ['#F6D6CB', '#EFC3B3', '#FBE7E0', '#E8B39F', '#F5CFC1', '#FCEEE8', '#E2A48E']}
FE_FILL = {'Fe0': ['#D6DBE2'], 'Fe2': ['#D4E3F2', '#C3D7EB', '#E0EBF6', '#B5CDE5', '#E8F0F9', '#CADCEF', '#ACC6E1'],
           'Fe3': ['#D9D6EC', '#C9C5E3', '#E4E1F2', '#BBB6DB', '#D1CDE8', '#ECEAF6'],
           'Fe6': ['#E6D2F0', '#F0E1F7']}
CU_LINE, FE_LINE = '#9E4A16', '#26527F'
CU_TEXT, FE_TEXT = '#6E3410', '#1D3F63'

FIGW, FIGH = 10.5, 7.4
MARG = dict(left=0.075, right=0.985, bottom=0.085, top=0.975)
AXW = FIGW*(MARG['right']-MARG['left']); AXH = FIGH*(MARG['top']-MARG['bottom'])
IN_PER_PH = AXW/14.0; IN_PER_V = AXH/2.5
SAMPLING = [dE*IN_PER_V, dpH*IN_PER_PH]   # inches per grid step (rows=E, cols=pH)

def assign_colors(L, fills):
    labs = [k for k, _ in collections.Counter(L.ravel()).most_common()]
    used = collections.defaultdict(int); cmap = {}
    for k in labs:
        st = STATE.get(names[k], 'Cu2')
        pal = fills[st]; cmap[k] = pal[used[st] % len(pal)]; used[st] += 1
    return cmap

def boundary_pixels(L, dil=3):
    b = np.zeros_like(L, dtype=bool)
    b[:, 1:] |= L[:, 1:] != L[:, :-1]
    b[1:, :] |= L[1:, :] != L[:-1, :]
    return ndimage.binary_dilation(b, iterations=dil)

def draw_fills(ax, L, cmap):
    labs = sorted(cmap.keys())
    idx = {k: i for i, k in enumerate(labs)}
    img = np.vectorize(idx.get)(L)
    ax.imshow(img, origin='lower', extent=ext, aspect='auto', interpolation='nearest',
              cmap=ListedColormap([cmap[k] for k in labs]), vmin=-0.5, vmax=len(labs)-0.5, zorder=0)

def draw_lines(ax, L, color, lw=1.4, z=3, sigma=0.9):
    pad = 3
    X = np.concatenate([pHs[0]-dpH*np.arange(pad, 0, -1), pHs, pHs[-1]+dpH*np.arange(1, pad+1)])
    Y = np.concatenate([Es[0]-dE*np.arange(pad, 0, -1), Es, Es[-1]+dE*np.arange(1, pad+1)])
    for k in np.unique(L):
        m = np.pad((L == k).astype(float), pad, mode='edge')
        ms = ndimage.gaussian_filter(m, sigma=sigma)
        if ms.max() < 0.5: continue
        ax.contour(X, Y, ms, levels=[0.5], colors=[color], linewidths=lw, zorder=z)

class Placer:
    """Collision-aware label placement using distance transforms in inches."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.rects = []   # (x0,x1,y0,y1) in data units
    def text_size(self, txt, fs):
        # rough footprint: mathtext markup removed
        core = txt.replace('$', '').replace('^', '').replace('_', '').replace('{', '').replace('}', '')
        w_in = 0.62*fs/72*len(core) + 0.1
        h_in = 1.25*fs/72 + 0.08
        return w_in/IN_PER_PH, h_in/IN_PER_V
    def place(self, mask, obstacles, txt, fs, other_rects=()):
        m = mask & ~obstacles
        if m.sum() < 3: m = mask
        mp = np.pad(m.astype(float), 1, constant_values=0)
        dt = ndimage.distance_transform_edt(mp, sampling=SAMPLING)[1:-1, 1:-1]
        w, h = self.text_size(txt, fs)
        need = 0.5*np.hypot(w*IN_PER_PH, h*IN_PER_V)
        order = np.argsort(dt.ravel())[::-1]
        best = None
        for flat in order[:4000]:
            v = dt.ravel()[flat]
            if v <= 0: break
            i, j = np.unravel_index(flat, dt.shape)
            x, y = pHs[j], Es[i]
            r = (x-w/2, x+w/2, y-h/2, y+h/2)
            if best is None: best = r
            ok = all(not (r[0] < q[1]+0.15 and r[1] > q[0]-0.15 and r[2] < q[3]+0.02 and r[3] > q[2]-0.02)
                     for q in list(self.rects)+list(other_rects))
            inside = (r[0] >= 0.05 and r[1] <= 13.95 and r[2] >= -0.98 and r[3] <= 1.48)
            if ok and inside:
                best = r; break
        x = (best[0]+best[1])/2; y = (best[2]+best[3])/2
        self.rects.append(best)
        return x, y

def draw_labels(ax, L, color, placer, obstacles=None, min_area=0.0015, fs=10, italic=False, special=None):
    c = collections.Counter(L.ravel())
    obstacles = np.zeros(L.shape, bool) if obstacles is None else obstacles
    for k, v in sorted(c.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
        if v / L.size < min_area: continue
        m = (L == k)
        txt = PRETTY.get(names[k], names[k])
        fsz = fs if v/L.size > 0.01 else fs-1.5
        if special and names[k] in special:
            x, y = special[names[k]]
        else:
            x, y = placer.place(m, obstacles, txt, fsz)
        ax.text(x, y, txt, color=color, fontsize=fsz, ha='center', va='center',
                fontstyle='italic' if italic else 'normal', zorder=5,
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.18', fc='white', ec='none', alpha=0.78))

def water(ax):
    x = np.array([0, 14])
    ax.plot(x, 1.229-0.05916*x, '--', color='#6B6B6B', lw=1, zorder=2)
    ax.plot(x, -0.05916*x, '--', color='#6B6B6B', lw=1, zorder=2)
    ang = np.degrees(np.arctan(-0.05916*IN_PER_V/IN_PER_PH))
    ax.text(0.2, 1.229-0.05916*0.2+0.035, r'O$_2$ / H$_2$O', color='#555', fontsize=8.5, rotation=ang, rotation_mode='anchor', zorder=6)
    ax.text(0.2, -0.05916*0.2+0.035, r'H$_2$O / H$_2$', color='#555', fontsize=8.5, rotation=ang, rotation_mode='anchor', zorder=6)

def frame(ax):
    ax.set_xlim(0, 14); ax.set_ylim(-1.0, 1.5)
    ax.set_xlabel('pH', fontsize=11); ax.set_ylabel('E / V vs SHE', fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xticks(range(0, 15, 1)); ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-1.0, 1.51, 0.25))
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=9, colors='#333')
    for s in ax.spines.values(): s.set_color('#444')

def newfig():
    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(FIGW, FIGH), dpi=100)
    ax = fig.add_axes([MARG['left'], MARG['bottom'], MARG['right']-MARG['left'], MARG['top']-MARG['bottom']])
    return fig, ax

cu_cmap = assign_colors(lab[0], CU_FILL); fe_cmap = assign_colors(lab[1], FE_FILL)
cu_obst = boundary_pixels(lab[0]); fe_obst = boundary_pixels(lab[1])

# ---- Joint diagram ----
fig, ax = newfig()
draw_fills(ax, lab[0], cu_cmap)
draw_lines(ax, lab[0], CU_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_lines(ax, lab[1], FE_LINE, lw=1.5)
pl = Placer()
draw_labels(ax, lab[0], CU_TEXT, pl, obstacles=fe_obst, fs=10.5)
draw_labels(ax, lab[1], FE_TEXT, pl, obstacles=cu_obst, fs=10, italic=True)
water(ax); frame(ax)
fig.savefig('joint.svg'); fig.savefig('joint.png', dpi=110)

# ---- Cu-only ----
fig, ax = newfig()
draw_fills(ax, lab[0], cu_cmap); draw_lines(ax, lab[0], CU_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_labels(ax, lab[0], CU_TEXT, Placer(), fs=11, min_area=0.0003); water(ax); frame(ax)
fig.savefig('cu.svg'); fig.savefig('cu.png', dpi=110)

# ---- Fe-only ----
fig, ax = newfig()
draw_fills(ax, lab[1], fe_cmap); draw_lines(ax, lab[1], FE_LINE, lw=1.3)
draw_labels(ax, lab[1], FE_TEXT, Placer(), fs=11, min_area=0.0003); water(ax); frame(ax)
fig.savefig('fe.svg'); fig.savefig('fe.png', dpi=110)

json.dump({'left': MARG['left'], 'right': MARG['right'], 'bottom': MARG['bottom'], 'top': MARG['top'],
           'figw': FIGW, 'figh': FIGH}, open('axes_geom.json', 'w'))
print('done')

content.text:
Here is where the work stands. The solver, the full 281 × 251 E–pH grid (70,531 points, all converged), the region/boundary/junction extraction, and the three matplotlib SVG figures (joint, Cu-only, Fe-only) are complete and checked visually; the HTML page has not been assembled yet, so the results are reported here directly.

## System and conventions

1 mM Cu(II), 1 mM Fe(III), 10 mM citrate, 10 mM glycine, 0.1 M Cl⁻, 0.1 M NH₃(total), 25 °C, I = 0.1 m. All log K at I = 0 (MINTEQ v4, NIST 46 for ammines/Cu(I), a few additions), Davies coefficients at I = 0.1 (log γ = −0.107·z²). Predominance = species holding the largest share of the metal (solids counted stoichiometrically); a line is where the two named species have equal share, which is why, e.g., the Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ line sits at +0.735 V rather than the nominal 0.771 V (activity coefficients plus Fe³⁺ being only ~46 % of Fe(III) because of FeCl²⁺ and FeHCit⁺).

## How Cu and Fe partition

**Copper.** Under oxidizing conditions Cu(II) walks through four ligands with pH: Cu²⁺ (pH < 3.2; CuCl⁺ ~5 %) → CuCit⁻ (3.2–6.2; Cu₂Cit₂²⁻ ~11 %, Cu(Cit)₂⁴⁻ ~6 %) → Cu(Gly)₂ (6.2–11.2, > 99 % at pH 9) → CuO (pH > 11.2). Cu(II) ammines never predominate — glycinate beats them by 3–4 log units. A Cu(I) window exists only where Cl⁻ or NH₃ can stabilize it: CuCl₂⁻ (pH 0–5.3, E 0.12–0.33 V) and Cu(NH₃)₂⁺ (pH 7.1–11.6, E ≈ −0.2 to +0.05 V); between pH 5.3 and 7.1 Cu(I) disproportionates and Cu(II) reduces straight to Cu(s). Cu₂O appears only at pH > 11.6; CuCl(s) never forms. Cu(s) covers everything below ≈ +0.12 V (acid) to ≈ −0.2 V (alkaline).

**Iron.** Fe(III): Fe³⁺ (pH < 1.4) → FeCit (1.4–2.5) → Fe(OH)Cit⁻ (2.5–7.0) → ferrihydrite (pH > 7.0; onset of saturation pH 6.9) → FeO₄²⁻ above E = 2.06 − 0.098·pH (pH > 7). Fe(II): Fe²⁺ (pH < 3.7) → FeHCit (3.7–4.0) → FeCit⁻ (4–9.5) → Fe(Gly)₂ (9.5–10.4) → Fe(OH)₂(s) (10.4–12) → Fe(OH)₃⁻ (> 12). Fe(s) below −0.556 V (acid) sloping to −0.93 V at pH 14. Citrate keeps Fe(III) soluble to pH 7 and Fe(II) soluble to pH 10.4; glycine matters for Fe only in the narrow Fe(Gly)₂ window.

## Principal boundaries (solver-fitted; E in V vs SHE)

Cu: Cu²⁺/CuCl₂⁻ E = 0.325 (pH 0–3.1); CuCl₂⁻/Cu(s) E = 0.124 (pH 0–5.3); Cu²⁺/CuCit⁻ pH 3.18 (CuHCit sliver 3.13–3.17); CuCit⁻/CuCl₂⁻ E = 0.614 − 0.0956 pH; CuCit⁻/Cu(s) E = 0.242 − 0.0234 pH (pH 5.35–6.15); CuCit⁻/Cu(Gly)₂ pH 6.18; Cu(Gly)₂/Cu(s) E = 0.424 − 0.0524 pH (6.2–7.05); Cu(Gly)₂/Cu(NH₃)₂⁺ E = 0.154 − 0.0127 pH (7.1–11.2); Cu(NH₃)₂⁺/Cu(s) curved, ≈ −0.118 V/pH below the NH₄⁺ pKa flattening to −0.20 V above pH 9.5; Cu(Gly)₂/CuO pH 11.18; Cu(NH₃)₂⁺/Cu₂O pH 11.58; Cu₂O/CuO E = 0.655 − 0.0593 pH; Cu(s)/Cu₂O E = 0.476 − 0.0591 pH.

Fe: Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ E = 0.735 (pH 0–1.35); Fe³⁺/FeCit pH 1.38–1.42; Fe²⁺/FeCit E = 0.979 − 0.173 pH; FeCit/Fe(OH)Cit⁻ pH 2.48; Fe²⁺/Fe(OH)Cit⁻ E = 1.045 − 0.200 pH; Fe²⁺/FeHCit pH 3.68; FeHCit/FeCit⁻ pH 3.98; Fe(OH)Cit⁻/FeCit⁻ E = 0.511 − 0.0592 pH; Fe(OH)Cit⁻/ferrihydrite pH 7.03; FeCit⁻/ferrihydrite E = 1.334 − 0.176 pH; FeO₄²⁻/ferrihydrite E = 2.061 − 0.0983 pH; Fe²⁺/Fe(s) E = −0.556; FeCit⁻/Fe(s) E = −0.557 − 0.0104 pH; FeCit⁻/Fe(Gly)₂ pH 9.52; Fe(Gly)₂/Fe(OH)₂ pH 10.38; ferrihydrite/Fe(OH)₂ E = 0.159 − 0.0593 pH; Fe(s)/Fe(OH)₂ E = −0.047 − 0.0590 pH; Fe(OH)₂/Fe(OH)₃⁻ pH 12.03; ferrihydrite/Fe(OH)₃⁻ E = −0.555; Fe(OH)₃⁻/Fe(s) E = 0.314 − 0.0891 pH.

## Junctions (pH, E; ±0.03, ±0.005)

Cu: (3.15, 0.325) Cu²⁺/CuCit⁻/CuCl₂⁻; (5.33, 0.115) CuCit⁻/CuCl₂⁻/Cu; (6.18, 0.095) CuCit⁻/Cu(Gly)₂/Cu; (7.08, 0.055) Cu(Gly)₂/Cu(NH₃)₂⁺/Cu; (11.22, 0.015) Cu(Gly)₂/Cu(NH₃)₂⁺/CuO; (11.58, −0.035) Cu(NH₃)₂⁺/Cu₂O/CuO; (11.58, −0.205) Cu(NH₃)₂⁺/Cu/Cu₂O.
Fe: (1.4, 0.735) Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺/FeCit; (2.48, 0.555) Fe²⁺/FeCit/Fe(OH)Cit⁻; (3.73, 0.305) Fe²⁺/Fe(OH)Cit⁻/FeHCit; (3.98, 0.275) Fe(OH)Cit⁻/FeCit⁻/FeHCit; (3.67, −0.565) and (3.98, −0.575) with Fe(s); (6.98, 1.385) FeO₄²⁻/HFeO₄⁻/Fe(OH)Cit⁻; (7.12, 1.355) FeO₄²⁻/Fe(OH)Cit⁻/ferrihydrite; (7.12, 0.095) Fe(OH)Cit⁻/FeCit⁻/ferrihydrite; (9.53, −0.335) and (9.53, −0.645); (10.38, −0.455) and (10.38, −0.655); (12.03, −0.555) and (12.03, −0.755).
Notable Cu/Fe crossings: Cu(Gly)₂/Cu(NH₃)₂⁺ × FeCit⁻/ferrihydrite (7.3, 0.055); CuCit⁻/Cu(Gly)₂ × Fe(OH)Cit⁻/FeCit⁻ (6.18, 0.145); Cu(Gly)₂/CuO × FeO₄²⁻/ferrihydrite (11.18, 0.96).

## Key constants in the solver

E°: Cu²⁺/Cu⁺ 0.159, Cu²⁺/Cu 0.339, Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ 0.771, Fe²⁺/Fe −0.447, FeO₄²⁻/Fe³⁺ 2.20 V (less certain). log β: CuCit⁻ 7.57, Cu(Gly)₂ 15.7, Cu(NH₃)₄²⁺ 11.75, CuCl₂⁻ 5.42 (from Cu⁺), Cu(NH₃)₂⁺ 10.86, FeCit 13.1, Fe(OH)Cit⁻ 10.5 (added; FeCit pKa 2.6, less certain), FeCit⁻ 6.1, Fe(Gly)₂ 8.29; log K_sp-type: ferrihydrite 3.191, CuO 7.644, Cu₂O −1.406, Fe(OH)₂ 13.564. Ligand pKa: citrate 3.13/4.76/6.40, glycine 2.35/9.78, NH₄⁺ 9.24.

## Caveats

Aged Fe oxides (goethite, hematite, magnetite), Cu(OH)₂, Cu-Fe ferrites, polynuclear Fe-citrate and Cu-citrate hydroxo species are excluded; goethite/hematite would greatly expand the Fe(III) solid field, polynuclear Fe-citrate would extend Fe(III) solubility to ~pH 9, and a CuCitH₋₁ species would push the CuCit⁻/Cu(Gly)₂ line to ~pH 8.5. Ligands are treated as redox-inert; I is held at 0.1 even at pH 0 and 14. Solid saturation onsets sit ≤ 0.02 V / 0.25 pH before the drawn 50 % lines.

I have the three figures rendered and the tables assembled; I can publish the page with the interactive diagrams and full constant/boundary tables next.
